newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban say they capture eastern Afghan province.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say they capture eastern Afghan province.

text.p: The rebel Taleban Islamic militia has captured an eastern Afghan province after heavy fighting with pro-government Hezb-i-Islami forces, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said on Sunday.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Taleban sources as saying the Islamic fighters seized the city of Asadabad, capital of Kunar province on Saturday night after an intense battle.
The Taleban said they had taken control of the capital and seized a large number of tanks, artillery and other weapons.
Heavy fighting had been reported between Taleban and Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-e-Islami faction in Shewa, about 25 km (16 miles) north of Jalalabad since Friday morning.
AIP said Sher Afzal, a prominent Hezb-i-Islami commander, was killed in the fighting on Saturday.

The Taleban, seeking to overthrow the Kabul government led by President Burhanuddin Rabbani and install a purist Islamic order, have been tightening their grip on eastern Afghanistan since seizing the strategic city of Jalalabad on September 11.
